name: Epsilon-lexicase GP
tagline: Standard GP operators with epsilon-lexicase selection: filter candidates case-by-case using min-error + MAD epsilon.
pseudocode:
1. Score each tree by MSE on $X,y$; cache per-case absolute errors $E\!\in\!\mathbb R^{P\times n}$.
2. To pick a parent:
3. \quad Candidates $\leftarrow$ all trees; shuffle the $n$ training cases.
4. \quad For each case in shuffled order (until $|$candidates$|\le 1$):
5. \quad\quad $\epsilon \leftarrow \mathrm{MAD}(E_{\text{cand},c})$, $e_{\min}\leftarrow\min E_{\text{cand},c}$.
6. \quad\quad Keep candidates with $E_{\text{cand},c}\le e_{\min}+\epsilon$ (semi-dynamic lexicase).
7. \quad Return random survivor.
8. Variation: subtree crossover ($p{=}0.9$), subtree mutation ($p{=}0.05$), elitism on raw MSE.
diff_from_baseline: Spector (2012); La Cava, Spector, Helmuth, 'Epsilon-Lexicase Selection for Regression' (GECCO 2016/2019). Selects parents that excel on individual cases instead of aggregate fitness, preserving solution diversity.

name: Parsimony-pressure GP
tagline: Standard tournament GP plus an adaptive parsimony coefficient (gplearn 'auto' rule) penalizing tree length during selection.
pseudocode:
1. Compute raw fitness $f_i =\!\text{MSE}(\text{tree}_i,X,y)$ and length $\ell_i$.
2. Adaptive coefficient: $c=\mathrm{Cov}(\ell,f)/\mathrm{Var}(\ell)$, clamp to $[0, 10^{-3}]$.
3. Penalized fitness: $\tilde f_i = f_i + c\cdot \ell_i$ (used only for selection).
4. Elitism by raw $f$ (best-fit tree always preserved).
5. Tournament selection (size 7) on $\tilde f$.
6. Subtree crossover ($p{=}0.9$) / mutation ($p{=}0.05$); reject children with depth $>17$.
diff_from_baseline: Poli, Langdon, McPhee, 'A Field Guide to Genetic Programming' (2008); gplearn auto-parsimony reference (parsimony_coefficient='auto'). Standard bloat-control baseline.

name: Standard GP
tagline: Koza-style GP: tournament selection, subtree crossover/mutation, raw MSE fitness, depth-capped trees, elitism.
pseudocode:
1. Evaluate fitness $f_i = \text{MSE}(\text{tree}_i, X, y)$.
2. Elitism: copy best tree to next generation.
3. While population not full:
4. \quad $r \sim \mathrm{Uniform}(0,1)$.
5. \quad If $r<0.9$: pick 2 parents by tournament (size 7), apply subtree crossover.
6. \quad Else if $r<0.95$: pick 1 parent, apply subtree mutation (replace random subtree with a 'grow'-tree of depth 3).
7. \quad Else: clone the parent.
8. \quad Reject children with depth $>17$.
diff_from_baseline: Koza, 'Genetic Programming' (1992); the canonical tree-GP reference. Default symbolic-regression baseline before complexity control or selection-rule changes.
